Balita

Weak peso on the table for DBCC

The weak peso will be part of the government's year-end economic review, the Department of Budget and Management says. The review is run by the Development Budget Coordination Committee (DBCC), the group of agencies that sets the government's official assumptions for growth, prices and the exchange rate. It is expected to meet in the third week of December. Budget Secretary Kim Robert C. De Leon said all economic indicators, local and international, will be looked at, but he did not want to preempt the decision. The DBCC had projected the peso to average P60-P62 to the dollar this year, and the peso has been trading weaker than that range. Today's rate is in the peso box. Growth is the other concern: the economy grew just 2.1% in July to September, bringing nine-month growth to 2.5%, below the 3.5%-4.5% full-year target. Still unknown: whether the targets and assumptions will change, and by how much. BusinessWorld: Weak peso expected to factor into DBCC outlook

Economy Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan has said the economy would need to grow about 6.3% in the fourth quarter just to reach the lower end of the full-year target. BusinessWorld: Weak peso expected to factor into DBCC outlook

Para sa pamilya: A weaker peso means each dollar sent home converts to more pesos, but the remittance fee still matters, so check it each time you send.

70 OFWs return from Saudi Arabia

Seventy OFWs from Saudi Arabia landed at NAIA Terminal 3 on November 13, the Department of Migrant Workers (DMW) said on Saturday, as tensions in the Middle East continue. The DMW says up to 1,170 OFWs and their dependents have been brought home so far, working with the Overseas Workers Welfare Administration (OWWA), the agency that runs welfare programs for OFWs. Those arriving were met with help under UPLIFT (Unified Package for Livelihoods, Industry, Food, and Transport), the government program for Filipino households affected by the conflict. The help included medical and financial aid, transport to their provinces, and other support. The Manila International Airport Authority also gave medical assistance. What the coverage does not say: how much financial aid each worker received, and how many more flights home are planned. GMA Pinoy Abroad: 70 OFWs from Saudi Arabia return to PH amid Middle East crisis -- DMW

Inquirer Global Nation also reports the arrivals: 70 OFWs from Saudi Arabia return home amid Middle East tensions

Para sa pamilya: If a family member comes home from the Middle East, ask DMW and OWWA about UPLIFT: medical, financial and transport help to the province.

PH explores backup oil abroad

State-run PNOC Exploration Corp. has signed letters of intent, which are preliminary agreements, with Indonesia's PT Interport Mandiri Utama and The Shell Co. of Thailand Ltd. to explore "oil ticketing". Under this setup, a country pays for the right to draw on oil stored in another country during an emergency, under agreed conditions. Pilot projects would use existing storage in Indonesia and Thailand, which could offer an alternative to building new tanks and buying oil stocks upfront. The move comes as the months-long Middle East war keeps disrupting fuel supply. PNOC is separately building government oil reserves, with the first storage tank targeted by end-2027, though critics warn those costs could eventually be passed on to consumers. A study by the Economic Research Institute for ASEAN and East Asia says the region could save about $610 million a year by raising joint reserves from 10 to 30 days. Still unknown: the cost to the Philippines and when the pilots start. PhilStar Business: Philippines tapping oil stocks in Thailand, Indonesia

Para sa pamilya: No pump price change comes from this yet; it is about fuel supply in an emergency, and any cost to consumers is still unknown.

Check bank hours before going out

Today to November 18 is a special non-working holiday in Metro Manila for the Asean Summit, under Proclamation 1447, and many bank branches will close or keep shorter hours. BPI says all its Metro Manila branches stay open, though operations may be adjusted for road closures. UnionBank keeps 12 NCR branches open, Metrobank closes 14, PNB's selected branches open 9 a.m. to noon, and AUB's 28 selected NCR branches open 9 a.m. to 3 p.m. Before the family goes out to claim padala or pay bills, check your bank's official page, or use ATMs and apps. Manila Times: Banks set branch schedules for Asean Summit holiday

Para sa pamilya: In Metro Manila from Nov. 16 to 18, check your bank's branch list before going; many banks say ATMs and apps remain available.

Fuel price rollback: An industry source estimates another rollback, meaning a price cut, in the coming week: diesel down P4.50 to P4.80 per liter and gasoline down P2.70 to P3.00 per liter. These are estimates; oil firms announce official prices on Monday, effective the next day. GMA Money: Another fuel price rollback expected next week

Cheaper airfares: The Civil Aeronautics Board approved lower fuel surcharges, the extra fee added to tickets for fuel costs, for November 16 to 30. The exact amounts are not in our material. Inquirer Business: Filipinos to enjoy cheaper airfares from Nov 16-30

Stock market dips: The PSEi, the main index of the Philippine stock market, ended last week at 5,593.49, down 2.92 percent and at its weakest close in almost a year, amid worries about stagflation, which means slow growth combined with high prices. Manila Times: PSEi faces downside on stagflation fears
